title: Trump to visit Kansas as Republicans campaign ahead of midterm elections
text:
Trump to visit Kansas as Republicans campaign ahead of midterm elections
President Donald Trump will return to Kansas to support Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections. Vice President JD Vance addressed fuel prices during a recent visit, while the Sternberg Museum remains open after receiving donor support. Early voting is underway nationwide, and a lawsuit over the Kansas City Chiefs stadium project has been settled.
October 28 — President Donald Trump is scheduled to make a second visit to Kansas this Saturday to support Republican politicians in the state. The visit is part of a series of appearances by top Republicans ahead of the November 3 midterm election, with events drawing large crowds in Olathe, the Wichita area, and Topeka. Trump is expected to appear in Salina, where he will campaign for U.S. Senator Roger Marshall and other Republican candidates, including gubernatorial candidate Ty Masterson.
Vice President JD Vance recently spoke in Topeka, where he attributed rising gasoline and diesel prices in Kansas to "tinpot dictators" in the Middle East, former President Joe Biden, and other Democrats. Vance did not mention President Trump or Republicans in Congress as contributing to higher fuel prices during his speech, which was intended to support Senator Marshall in his race against Democrat Adam Hamilton.
In other state news, the Sternberg Museum of Natural History at Fort Hays State University will remain open after donors contributed $1.2 million to cover operating expenses. University president Tisa Mason informed a legislative committee of the museum's reprieve, though legislators questioned her handling of the closure announcement and the decision to remove the museum from the university's budget.
A lawsuit filed by the Unified Government of Wyandotte County and Kansas City against the state of Kansas regarding the Kansas City Chiefs stadium project was settled on Friday. The local government had raised concerns about losing local control over the project.
Early voting has seen high turnout across the country, with tens of millions of Americans casting ballots in the midterm elections that will determine control of the House and Senate. The U.S. Department of Justice plans to send 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states, though specific locations have not been disclosed. The United States has extended a total of $14.2 billion in assistance to Ukraine, including direct budgetary support, humanitarian aid, and development aid aimed at strengthening Ukraine's energy infrastructure, according to the White House.
